newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Feb 10.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Westpac and Ansett are this week launching an Olympics Partner Visa card, to be followed by a Coles Myer Master Card, a combined Automobile Associations of Australia credit card and the Commonwealth Bank's first major co-branded card, in moves which will ee the already intensely competitive Australian credit card market hit by a second wave of co-branding and loyalty programmes. Page 1.

AMP group development manager Jonathan Schwartz has confirmed that AMP is considering joining a bidding war for the UK's Scottish Amicable life assurance group. AMP has openly shown its desire to purchase a UK life and pensions group and is expected to send in excess of A$6 billion overseas. Page 19.

Hastings Fund Management Ltd has launched a A$175 million fund to be known as the Australian Infrastructure Fund Limited. Hastings is raising the A$175 thorough the issue of stapled securities and Hasting's managing director Mike Fitzpatrick said there had already been strong interest from institutions, but says they are also looking to attract retail investors. Page 19.

U.S.-owned PGT Australia, a unit of Pacific Gas and Electric Corp, has asked the Western Australia Government for a licence to build the South West Australia Natural Gas pipeline. The A$1 billion plan which will duplicate the existing 1,600 km Dampier-to-Bunbury gas pipeline, plans to cut domestic gas prices by up to 30 percent, and is expected to be completed by January 1, 2000. Page 19.

National Australia Asset Management's managing director Paul Laband is planning to double the funds under management to A$10 billion by the year 2000 and to A$30 billion by 2005. The plan is built on a continuation of NAAM's good performance in the last to years and investing more in "non-traditional" assets. Page 20.

A Texaco and Mobil study of the Gorgon and Chrysaor gas fields off Western Australia is expected to show that independent development of the fields is economically possible. The estimated A$5 billion project was thought to be uneconomic without the help of the North-West Shelf LNG venture. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Western Australia Government has slammed a plan by U.S.-owned PGT Australia for the development of the A$1 billion South West Australia Natural Gas pipeline, which is expected to cut domestic gas prices by up to 30 per cent, calling the plan "provocative and not in the public interest." Page 29.

The collapse of a property and franchise marketing company associated with Craig Gore, the son of bankrupt Gold Coast property developer Mike Gore, is the focus of an investigation by the Australian Securities Commission. The ASC is investigating his business dealings and role in Cartergorical Pty Ltd, which was placed in voluntary administration by directors last November. Page 29.

World financial leaders at the Group of Seven meeting in Berlin have implied they would try to halt a rise in the U.S. dollar by indicating they wanted major exchange rates to stabilise around current levels. The leaders claim the U.S. dollar had climbed enough from its record lows of 1995 and called for currency stability to create conditions for world economic growth. Page 29.

AMP directors are months away from selecting a final demutualisation structure and although AMP members are aware of the company's A$1 billion demutualisation plan, they will receive little new information at April annual meeting. AMP chief executive George Trumbull said AMP would discuss some elements of the plan but was unlikely to reveal the structure for the allocation of shares. Page 29.

BHP chief executive John Prescott is not convinced that now is a good time to sell the BHP's 37 percent stake in Foster's Brewing Ltd. Speculation of such a sale has lifted Foster's shares 15 cents to A$2.65, valuing BHP's holding at around A$1.9 billion. Page 31.

When St George Bank Ltd reports its full-year profit results in September it will have some hard cost savings stemming from its recent merger with Advance Bank Australia Ltd. St George had already achieved A$10 million in cost savings from merging its treasury and capital markets operations. Page 30.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Investors' hunger for exposure to the booming infrastructure market will see a new A$175 million fund - the Australian Infrastructure Fund - hit the market in coming weeks. The fund's parent company, Hastings Fund Management, is planning to sell a broad range of infrastructure investments, including light rail, tollways, pipelines and power stations. Page 35.

BHP managing director John Prescott said yesterday that the company is examining the best way to capture the value of its A$2 billion investment in Foster's Brewing Group. Prescott said no final decision had been made on the company's 37 percent sharehlding in Foster's but says BHP is keen to take advantage of the brewer's strong share price performance over the past two years. Page 35.

Research by broker JB Were & Son has found that retail investors are selling shares to invest in cash because they fear a major market correction. The research revealed cash levels for retail investors held in brokers' cash management trusts were the highest in seven years. Page 35.

Lion Nathan's Australian head Gordon Cairns is attempting to get the brewer back on a competitive footing with Carlton United Breweries which to date has beaten the New Zealand-based Lion in both sales and development of new products. Cairn's priority is to halt the market share rout which he attributes to a lack of advertising back-up for core brands. Page 35.

Wesfarmers and Futuris Corp are expecting improved profits for the 1996/97 financial year with cost-cutting programmes offsetting falling farm incomes. Wesfarmers' interim net profit, due today, is expected to be between A$50 million and A$52 million, up A$38 million from last year. Page 38.
THE AGE

Melbourne-base infrastructure group Hastings Fund Management is to launch a diversified infrastructure investment vehicle under the name Australian Infrastructure Fund Ltd (AIF). The A$175 million AIF will include rail, road, gas and electricity assets in Victoria and three other states. Page C1.

Perth-based fashion chain Worth's and its Victorian trading partner Alexanders have been forced to appoint administrators due to the harsh retail trading environment. The company appointed Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu administrators on Friday. Page C1.

The American Electric Power Company has downgraded its planned involvement in bidding for the giant Loy Yang A power station in Victoria. The A$5 billion sale has deterred many international bidders because of the asset's sheer size, with uncertainty surrounding other co-bidders and possible buyers including California utility Pacific Gas and Electric. Page C2.

Research from retail stockbroker J.B. Were has found retail investors are selling out of the sharemarket to invest in cash. Cash levels in cash management trusts are at their highest in seven years at just under A$1.3 billion, up from A$850 million from last year. Investors are putting their money in high-yield or defensive stocks, fearing a stockmarket crash. Page C2.

Lion Nathan Australian brewing operations head Gordon Cairns is implementing a series of "quick fix" solutions to halt a market share slide. The first "quick fix" is an A$10 million new advertising campaign. Lion Nathan's market share could fall below 40 percent this financial year as rival brewer CUB climbs in sales and development of new products. Page C3.

A report from market forecaster BIS Shrapnel predicts rents and values of Melbourne industrial property to rise by up to 70 percent in the next 10 years. The report says there will be a strong rise in construction from next year as the low base for the Melbourne industrial property market comes off. Page C4.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
